headline: Britannia's towns get walls — and the goal-matrix registry gets a permanent audit
lede: Six of eight gate-towns in BRITANNIA now stand behind seeded stone rings with one gate you walk through, built on laws that refuse to strand a pilgrim or erase a road. On the research side, the held-out registry audit that was a session-memory note is now a check that runs on every matrix build.

notes.text: BRITANNIA #2538 (merged 88215bd, live): walls with one hash-chosen gate per town; the wall knocks with its own voice and a refusal names which side the gate standeth; classic mode stamps Origin's own BRICK.CON tileset held in the bundle since the audit.

The stage proved the remaining half of the gap is data-blocked, not laziness: every *.ULT region file in the jsdos bundle is terrain-only (1280 B) and no INSIDE.DAT ships — enterable buildings stay stage 2 by evidence.

retrogames-rl #9 (7835455): auditRegistry() cross-checks every goal-heldout entry against its model's training stamp on every matrix run; the pre-fix audit came back clean — no held-out ever burned at the wrong stamp. Matrix self-test now 12/12.
#2516 training remains honestly gated: goals/PREDICTIONS.md still waits on the #2529 answer (default A); the moment it lands, run3c.mjs --jobs 8 generates the whole matrix in one sitting.
